Two things I've noticed while working on this PR that might require a core HA change:

- When calling the reauth config flow, the HA UI shows a second instance of the component on the integrations page, the original and a second that says "Reconfigure". [See example here](https://i.imgur.com/FfBrRRA.jpg). This can be a bit confusing as it appears you have two instances of the integration. I think the desired behavior should be you only see one instance of the component (in this example) that shows the red border with "Reconfigure".
- When the reauth flow is executed, I'm running a check at the very end to see if a config entry already exists. If it does, the existing config entry is being updated and the config flow is aborted to prevent trying to create another config entry. Although the body of the dialog says "Re-authentication was successful", the title of the dialog says "Aborted" which can be a bit confusing. The desired behavior would be to have a custom title for the dialog that says "Success".
@shred86 Both points that you describe are expected, although I do agree that they don't present the cleanest user experience and might benefit from some more core thinking.

This integration should now meet all the criteria for the silver integration quality rating with the addition of handling expiration of auth credentials now:

- [x] Connection/configuration is handled via a component.
- [x] Set an appropriate SCAN_INTERVAL (if a polling integration)
- [x] Raise PlatformNotReady if unable to connect during platform setup (if appropriate)
- [x] **Handles expiration of auth credentials. Refresh if possible or print correct error and fail setup. If based on a config entry, should trigger a new config entry flow to re-authorize.**
- [x] Handles internet unavailable. Log a warning once when unavailable, log once when reconnected.
- [x] Handles device/service unavailable. Log a warning once when unavailable, log once when reconnected.
- [x] Set available property to False if appropriate
- [x] Entities have unique ID (if available)

Just pushed a refactor to hopefully make the code more logical and clear. The goal was to have step methods just handle displaying forms and setting variables based on user input while the "private" helper methods handle the rest of the work.

I'm not entirely sure why I can't combine `async_step_reauth` and `async_step_reauth_confirm`. I was under the impression when "Reconfigure" is clicked in the UI, it would just call `async_step_reauth` again so I could just check `if user_input is None:` to display the MFA form. However, that doesn't seem to work and it seems all the other config flows I look at are split up like this as well.

> I worked around this by creating a separate user for Home Assistant (with a super long random password that I threw away).

Not sure if that’s any better than using my own account without 2FA. The attack vector is still there with your secondary account.

This is still an issue. Keep open.

In the enterprise world it's not uncommon to use "app passwords" for legacy things that do not support 2FA or modern authentication methods beyond user/password. As long as you use a complex password and you do not use that password anywhere else except for Home Assistant you will be safe. Set yourself a reminder to change the password every 90 days if you prefer extra caution. Make it 16 characters, random letters numbers and symbols. 

The ways a password are stolen include brute force using common passwords, a data leak that included login info and hackers use that info on other sites, man-in-the-middle if using a network that has been compromised, or keylogger. A strong password will prevent against brute force. Unique passwords will prevent a data-leak from compromising other accounts. MITM is becoming less common due to everything running  HTTPS but your own network can be trusted just don't log into this account from Starbucks. If there's a keylogger on the machine you used to setup Home Assistant you have bigger issues than Abode.

I noticed this method in the parent `ConfigFlow` class that some integrations use:

`_abort_if_unique_id_configured`

Is this the preferred method? As far as I can tell, it's essentially doing the same thing but with some more options (e.g. ability to update the existing flow).

I guess one different might be with Abode, we only want to allow users to add one Abode account where as other integrations might allow users to add multiple accounts for the same integration. I haven't been able to determine if it's possible with Abode yet but I just don't see it being something we need.
That abort helper will have a standard abort message. We want to use another message when reauthenticating.

This is just to check if the Abode integration is already set up. If it is, immediately abort the flow so the user can't set it up. After looking at it a little closer, it looks like `_abort_if_unique_id_configured` is only checking to see if that specific config flow already exists. Our case is a little different with Abode as we want to check to see if the integration has already been added, which I don't see a built in helper method for so I think this is fine.

Regarding reauth, my understanding is there's no way to change the title "Abort"... or is there? :grin:
`_abort_if_unique_id_configured` will check for config entries with same unique_id as the current flow and abort the flow if there's an existing entry that matches.

We don't allow moving to another step's form. The form is step specific and private to the step. Move between step by calling the step method. If we make this method a helper method instead of a step, it can be ok to keep it like this.
I think once I refactor this to be a helper method based on the feedback above, that should resolve this issue since this isn't actually a step.

@MartinHjelmare I'm assuming what you're mentioning in the other code comment I made is in reference to this block of code? As you mentioned and looking at `_abort_if_unique_id_configured` in the base `ConfigFlow` class, it looks like this is what `_abort_if_unique_id_configured` is doing but I just realized for users that have an existing Abode config flow, I don't think I was setting the `unique_id` property before so they're likely just set to `None`. I'm still looking into this but if that's the case, I'm guessing I'll need to add a check to update the users config flow with a `unique_id` if it doesn't already exist.

I this this part is ok for now.

You're correct that we should update the existing entries and make sure they have unique id set.
Please only wrap the line that can raise with try... except. Move this up just under the call to create the abode client.

I'm assuming `unique_id` for the config entry only has to be unique within the integration itself (i.e. unique to other Abode config entries) and all integrations. The username is the user's email address which could obviously be used for other integration logins.
